# `docstrings/` — docstring-normalization edge cases

Fixtures for [[adrs/ADR-0131-extract-python-code-docs-with-griffe-and-scope-dis]]
clause 9 (docstrings render fenced, with CRLF-to-LF, cleandoc and
trailing-whitespace normalization applied first) and the top README's R1/R2
rendering primitives. Every page under `expected/` was written by hand
against the top README's page contract; nothing here imports or runs
`griffe`, and no page was generated by a program.

## Sources

| Source | Exercises |
|---|---|
| `fences.py` | An embedded ` ``` ` fence plus a `~~~` fence inside one docstring (`has_both_fences`); a standalone run of four backticks (`has_four_backtick_run`); a standalone run of five backticks (`has_five_backtick_run`). Each proves R1's fence-sizing rule: n = max(3, longest backtick run in the normalized text + 1). |
| `headings_and_html.py` | A `# heading` line inside a docstring (`heading_case`); a NumPy-style section with a setext underline, `-----` (`numpy_style`); raw HTML — a `<div>` and an HTML comment (`html_case`). All three render verbatim inside the docstring's text fence; none is interpreted as page structure. |
| `empty_and_undocumented.py` | An empty docstring, `""""""` (`empty_docstring`), which normalizes to the empty string and renders `_Empty docstring._`; a member with no docstring at all (`no_docstring`), which renders `_Undocumented._`. |
| `whitespace.py` | A docstring body line carrying trailing spaces in source (`trailing_ws`), and the common 4-space code-block indentation `inspect.cleandoc` removes. Proves R2's per-line and whole-text trailing-whitespace strip runs after cleandoc, not instead of it. |
| `crlf_source.py` | Committed with LF line endings (git may normalize CRLF away on checkout, so a CRLF fixture cannot be committed as CRLF bytes directly). A test converts this file to CRLF bytes at test time, before rendering, and the expected page below is that CRLF-converted source's rendering — byte-identical to the LF source's own rendering, since R2 converts CRLF to LF before anything else, including line counting. |
| `async_function.py` | A module-scope `async def` (DL-4, 2026-09-25, dev-lead), added because no fixture set had one: `real/` and `nested/` exercise `async method` and `nested async function` respectively, but the plain `async function` kind had no golden anywhere in this tree. |

Every member above is a public, module-scope function; `include_private` plays
no role in this set's one scenario (no member here is private-named), so the
set does not separately exercise `include_private: false` — clause 4's
exclusion behavior is covered generically in `real/private-excluded`, per the
top README's note for `nested/all-included`.

## Scenario

One scenario only, per the assignment ("One scenario (include_private true)"):

`docstrings/all-included` — `include_private: true`, every source selected, one
page per source.

## Manifest configuration a test must use

```json
{"extractor": "python", "include_private": true, "glob": ["**/*.py"]}
```

`src/` is the fixture's repository root. A test runs the (future) dispatcher
with `--repo-root docstrings/src` and this language key, or an equivalent
in-process call, writing to a disposable output root — never inside this
fixture tree.

## CRLF test-time conversion (restates the top README's `crlf_source.py` note)

`crlf_source.py` is committed with LF endings under that name specifically so
a test can locate it and convert it. The conversion a test must perform:
read the committed bytes, replace every `\n` with `\r\n`, write those bytes to
a disposable copy, then run the extractor over that copy. The expected page,
`expected/all-included/python/crlf_source.py.md`, is unchanged by this
conversion — R2 normalizes `\r\n` back to `\n` before cleandoc, dedent, or
line counting, so the CRLF round-trip is invisible in the rendered output.
This was checked by hand: parsing the LF source and a `\r\n`-replaced,
`\r\n`→`\n`-normalized copy with stdlib `ast` yields identical `lineno`/
`end_lineno` values and an identical docstring string for `crlf_member`.

## ADR-silent decisions (set-level)

- **Fence content is plain prose, not a nested Markdown fence.** `fences.py`'s
  `has_four_backtick_run` and `has_five_backtick_run` embed their backtick
  runs as a run of literal backtick characters inside one line of prose
  (e.g. "a run of four backticks: ` ```` `.") rather than as a second nested
  fence block. Rationale: R1 sizes the outer fence from the longest
  consecutive backtick run *anywhere* in the normalized text, regardless of
  whether that run reads as a nested fence to a human; a bare run of
  backticks in prose is the simplest fixture that isolates the sizing rule
  from any other structural question (an actual nested fence is already
  covered, at n=3→4 sizing, by `has_both_fences` and by `synthetic/`'s
  `hazard` member).
- **One docstring exercises both the `` ``` `` and `~~~` cases together.**
  The assignment names both fence styles as one bullet ("a docstring
  containing an embedded ``` fence and a ~~~ fence"); this set reads that as
  one combined case in one member (`has_both_fences`), keeping the source
  count within the 6-source budget. Both fence styles are rendered verbatim,
  with no distinct handling for tilde fences: only backtick runs affect R1
  sizing, so the tilde fence's presence contributes nothing to `n` beyond
  what the backtick fence lines already require.
- **All members are top-level functions or the one added async function.**
  This set is only about docstring *text* normalization, not member kind,
  nesting or visibility, which the `nested/`, `real/` and `synthetic/` sets
  already cover; using one uniform kind (`function`, `public`) keeps each
  page's non-docstring bytes (signature, kind line) mechanical and lets a
  reviewer diff purely on the docstring-rendering bytes. `async_function.py`
  is the one exception, added after the fact to close the DL-4 module-scope
  `async def` coverage gap rather than to exercise docstring normalization;
  its docstring is plain prose with nothing to normalize.
